arguments.old_str:
# Ignition Perspective Human Verification

Use this optional test-only session when a reviewer wants to adjust approved PLC inputs and see
the resulting Logix Echo readbacks in a browser. Automated YAML cases remain the release gate.
This session is not a production HMI, commissioning substitute, or safety-validation tool.

## Architecture

```text
Perspective browser
        |
Ignition Gateway 8.3.8 in Docker
        | authenticated HTTP, one guarded transaction
Windows LogixEchoHarness bridge
        | allowlisted typed LDSDK reads and writes
FactoryTalk Logix Echo controller
```

Ignition does not receive a general PLC device connection. The generated Perspective project can
send only the keys in `tests/ignition/shd-lift-station.verify.yaml`. The bridge maps those keys to
exact LDSDK XPath addresses; the HTTP request cannot supply an address.

For each Apply action, the bridge:

1. Validates that every approved input is present and no unknown key was supplied.
2. Validates JSON types and numeric bounds.
3. Writes `LiftStationEnable = false` as the safe guard.
4. Writes non-guard inputs in manifest order.
5. Writes the requested enable value last.
6. Observes ten controller scans.
7. Reads all approved inputs and outputs and confirms the controller remains in Run.

Requests are serialized, so two Perspective actions cannot interleave writes.

## Prerequisites

- Complete [windows-runner-setup.md](windows-runner-setup.md), including the non-loopback Echo
  adapter and Rockwell VCS tools.
- Install Docker Desktop with Linux containers and either `docker compose` or `docker-compose`.
- Keep host ports `5095` and `9088` available, or pass different `-BridgePort` and
  `-GatewayPort` values.
- Review the [Ignition Docker image documentation](https://www.docs.inductiveautomation.com/docs/8.1/platform/docker-image)
  and the Inductive Automation EULA before accepting it.

The Compose service pins `inductiveautomation/ignition:8.3.8`, enables Perspective, seeds a
repository-local data directory on first run (`tests/ignition/.ignition-local/data`), and
bind-mounts the generated project from ignored `build/ignition/project`.

## Start

Set the EULA flag only after review. Optionally supply `GATEWAY_ADMIN_PASSWORD` in the current
shell; if omitted, the startup flow uses a local default (`localdev123!`) for convenience.

```powershell
$env:ACCEPT_IGNITION_EULA = "Y"

$securePassword = Read-Host "Temporary Ignition Gateway admin password" -AsSecureString
$passwordPointer = [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::SecureStringToBSTR($securePassword)
try {
    $env:GATEWAY_ADMIN_PASSWORD = `
        [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::PtrToStringBSTR($passwordPointer)
}
finally {
    [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::ZeroFreeBSTR($passwordPointer)
}

.\tests\ignition\start-verification.ps1
```

On first startup, the `ignition-init` service seeds `tests/ignition/.ignition-local/data` from
the container defaults. Later startups detect existing files and skip reseeding.

The start script requires `ACCEPT_IGNITION_EULA=Y` and then:

- Builds `build/SHD_BOI_Line.ACD` from the Rockwell VCS source.
- Builds the .NET harness and validates the verification manifest.
- Generates a cryptographic bridge token and the five-file Perspective project under `build/`.
- Creates and downloads a dedicated Echo chassis.
- Starts the authenticated bridge on the Windows host.
- Starts the pinned Ignition Gateway and waits for `/StatusPing`.

Open the URL printed by the script, normally:

```text
http://localhost:9088/data/perspective/client/ACS_Logix_Verification/
```

## Review procedure
arguments.new_str:
# Ignition Perspective Human Verification

Use this optional test-only session when a reviewer wants to adjust approved PLC inputs and see
the resulting Logix Echo readbacks in a browser. Automated YAML cases remain the release gate.
This session is not a production HMI, commissioning substitute, or safety-validation tool.

## Architecture

```text
Perspective browser
        |
Ignition Gateway 8.3.8 in Docker (project "Logix-Verification")
        | OPC UA device connection
FactoryTalk Logix Echo controller (ControlLogix 5580 emulation)
```

The Gateway runs from a single, hand-configured project named **`Logix-Verification`** with a
Perspective view named **`logix-verification`**. Unlike a generated one-off project, this Gateway
keeps a real Logix device connection so a reviewer (or an agent, via the Gateway config API) can
add tags and wire them into the view for whatever change is under review. There is no separate
Windows bridge process for this flow — Ignition talks to Echo directly over OPC UA/EtherNet-IP,
the same as it would talk to a physical controller.

## Prerequisites

- Complete [windows-runner-setup.md](windows-runner-setup.md), including the non-loopback Echo
  adapter and Rockwell VCS tools.
- Install Docker Desktop with Linux containers and either `docker compose` or `docker-compose`.
- Keep host port `9088` (HTTP) and `8043` (HTTPS) available, or set `IGNITION_HTTP_PORT` /
  `IGNITION_HTTPS_PORT` before starting.
- Review the [Ignition Docker image documentation](https://www.docs.inductiveautomation.com/docs/8.1/platform/docker-image)
  and the Inductive Automation EULA before accepting it.

The Compose service in [compose.yaml](../../tests/ignition/compose.yaml) pins
`inductiveautomation/ignition:8.3.8`, and bind-mounts two host directories:

| Host path | Container path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/ignition/seed/data` | `/usr/local/bin/ignition/data` | The Gateway's live data directory — raw files copied out of a configured container with `docker cp`. This is what makes the `Logix-Verification` project and its tag/device configuration persist and stay directly editable. |
| `tests/ignition/gwbk` | `/backups` (read-only) | Holds a checked-in `.gwbk` Gateway backup that can restore a fresh Gateway. Set `GATEWAY_RESTORE=/backups/<file>.gwbk` in `compose.yaml` to auto-restore on first boot of an empty `seed/data`. |

Neither directory is committed by default (raw Gateway data is a mutable local working copy, not
a source artifact) except the `.gwbk` backup, which is the durable, reviewable snapshot.

The API reference for the Gateway's config/scripting REST API is
[tests/ignition/ignition-openapi.json](../../tests/ignition/ignition-openapi.json) (large;
`grep` it rather than opening it whole). All API calls below need the header:

```text
X-Ignition-API-Token: Logix-Verification:qvJOLBrJNAFWrDgpYhtTBpKeGyPB1l6HxAabyf8SUjA
```

## Start

Set the EULA flag only after review. Optionally supply `GATEWAY_ADMIN_PASSWORD` in the current
shell; if omitted, Compose uses the default (`password`).

```powershell
$env:ACCEPT_IGNITION_EULA = "Y"
docker compose -f tests\ignition\compose.yaml up -d
```

Wait for the Gateway to accept API calls (module loading takes roughly a minute on first boot):

```powershell
do {
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 5
    $status = (curl.exe -s -o NUL -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:9088/StatusPing)
} while ($status -ne "200")
```

Open the project in a browser at:

```text
http://localhost:9088/data/perspective/client/Logix-Verification/logix-verification
```

## Verification procedure

Each PLC change under review follows this sequence. Steps 1–3 are one-time or per-change
Gateway configuration (done through the Gateway web UI at `http://localhost:9088`, or the config
REST API below); step 4 reloads the change; step 5 hands the session to the human reviewer.

### 1. Set up the Logix device connection to talk to the Echo emulator

In the Gateway web UI: **Config \> OPC UA \> Devices \> Create new Device \> Allen-Bradley Logix
Driver**. Point the connection at the Echo chassis's `EmulateEthernet\<ip>` comm path (see
[windows-runner-setup.md](windows-runner-setup.md) for how the non-loopback adapter IP is
assigned). Confirm the device reaches **Connected** status before continuing.

Equivalently, via the config API (`PUT /data/api/v1/resources/com.inductiveautomation.opcua/device`)
using the `X-Ignition-API-Token` header above — see the `device` tag in
[ignition-openapi.json](../../tests/ignition/ignition-openapi.json) for the request schema.

### 2. Add the tags needed to read for human verification

Add or update OPC tags in the `Logix-Verification` project's tag provider for every input and
output referenced by the change record, bound to the device from step 1. Do not invent tag paths —
read them from the exploded `src/` tree for the controller under review (per
[l5x-source.instructions.md](../../.github/instructions/l5x-source.instructions.md)). Use the
Gateway UI's Tag Browser, or `PUT /data/api/v1/resources/ignition/tag-provider` /
`POST /data/api/v1/tags/import` for scripted updates.

### 3. Modify the `logix-verification` view to include all the variables used in the testing setup

Edit the Perspective view at
`tests/ignition/seed/data/projects/Logix-Verification/com.inductiveautomation.perspective/views/logix-verification/view.json`
(or the Designer) so every tag added in step 2 has a bound component — readouts for outputs,
input controls for anything the reviewer needs to change. Keep the view scoped to the current
change; remove bindings for tags that are no longer relevant so the reviewer isn't looking at
stale data.

### 4. Initiate a project scan to load in the changed files

Because the view and tag files were edited directly on disk, tell the Gateway to pick them up:

```powershell
curl.exe -X POST `
  -H "X-Ignition-API-Token: Logix-Verification:qvJOLBrJNAFWrDgpYhtTBpKeGyPB1l6HxAabyf8SUjA" `
  http://localhost:9088/data/api/v1/scan/projects
```

Poll `GET /data/api/v1/scan/projects` (same header) until `scanActive` is `false`, then confirm
`lastScanTimestamp` advanced. If a resource lock is held, `POST` also releases it.

### 5. Inform the user the verification view is ready for review

Once the scan completes, tell the reviewer the view is ready and share the URL:

```text
http://localhost:9088/data/perspective/client/Logix-Verification/logix-verification
```

## Review procedure

`grep` it rather than opening it whole). All API calls below need the header:


Set the EULA flag only after review. Optionally supply `GATEWAY_ADMIN_PASSWORD` in the current

Wait for the Gateway to accept API calls (module loading takes roughly a minute on first boot):

```powershell

    Start-Sleep -Seconds 5
    $status = (curl.exe -s -o NUL -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:9088/StatusPing)
} while ($status -ne "200")
```

Open the project in a browser at:

```text

```

Each PLC change under review follows this sequence. Steps 1–3 are one-time or per-change
Gateway configuration (done through the Gateway web UI at `http://localhost:9088`, or the config
REST API below); step 4 reloads the change; step 5 hands the session to the human reviewer.

output referenced by the change record, bound to the device from step 1. Do not invent tag paths —

[l5x-source.instructions.md](../../.github/instructions/l5x-source.instructions.md)). Use the
Gateway UI's Tag Browser, or `PUT /data/api/v1/resources/ignition/tag-provider` /
`POST /data/api/v1/tags/import` for scripted updates.

`tests/ignition/seed/data/projects/Logix-Verification/com.inductiveautomation.perspective/views/logix-verification/view.json`
(or the Designer) so every tag added in step 2 has a bound component — readouts for outputs,
input controls for anything the reviewer needs to change. Keep the view scoped to the current
change; remove bindings for tags that are no longer relevant so the reviewer isn't looking at
stale data.

```powershell

  http://localhost:9088/data/api/v1/scan/projects
 ```

`lastScanTimestamp` advanced. If a resource lock is held, `POST` also releases it.

Once the scan completes, tell the reviewer the view is ready and share the URL:

```text
http://localhost:9088/data/perspective/client/Logix-Verification/logix-verification
 ```

## Review procedure

The reviewer works directly in the `logix-verification` Perspective view: adjust any bound
input controls, observe the bound output readouts, and compare against the change record's
expected behavior. This is a human observation, not an automated pass/fail — the persisted HTML
report from the YAML/Echo run in [tests/cases/](../../tests/cases) remains the auditable
expected-versus-actual automated evidence.

## Stop

```powershell
docker compose -f tests\ignition\compose.yaml down
```

`tests/ignition/seed/data` is retained on disk for faster later startup, so tags, the device
connection, and view edits persist across restarts. Remove it explicitly when a clean Gateway is
required (for example, to test restoring `tests/ignition/gwbk/*.gwbk` from scratch):

```powershell
Remove-Item tests\ignition\seed\data -Recurse -Force
```

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Action |
|---|---|
| `docker` not found | Install or start Docker Desktop, then confirm `docker compose version` |
| Gateway never reaches `StatusPing` | Run `docker compose -f tests/ignition/compose.yaml logs gateway` |

result.content:
1. # Ignition Perspective Human Verification
2. 
3. Use this optional test-only session when a reviewer wants to adjust approved PLC inputs and see
4. the resulting Logix Echo readbacks in a browser. Automated YAML cases remain the release gate.
5. This session is not a production HMI, commissioning substitute, or safety-validation tool.
6. 
7. ## Architecture
8. 
9. ```text
10. Perspective browser
11.         |
12. Ignition Gateway 8.3.8 in Docker (project "Logix-Verification")
13.         | OPC UA device connection
14. FactoryTalk Logix Echo controller (ControlLogix 5580 emulation)
15. ```
16. 
17. The Gateway runs from a single, hand-configured project named **`Logix-Verification`** with a
18. Perspective view named **`logix-verification`**. Unlike a generated one-off project, this Gateway
19. keeps a real Logix device connection so a reviewer (or an agent, via the Gateway config API) can
20. add tags and wire them into the view for whatever change is under review. There is no separate
21. Windows bridge process for this flow — Ignition talks to Echo directly over OPC UA/EtherNet-IP,
22. the same as it would talk to a physical controller.
23. 
24. ## Prerequisites
25. 
26. - Complete [windows-runner-setup.md](windows-runner-setup.md), including the non-loopback Echo
27.   adapter and Rockwell VCS tools.
28. - Install Docker Desktop with Linux containers and either `docker compose` or `docker-compose`.
29. - Keep host port `9088` (HTTP) and `8043` (HTTPS) available, or set `IGNITION_HTTP_PORT` /
30.   `IGNITION_HTTPS_PORT` before starting.
31. - Review the [Ignition Docker image documentation](https://www.docs.inductiveautomation.com/docs/8.1/platform/docker-image)
32.   and the Inductive Automation EULA before accepting it.
33. 
34. The Compose service in [compose.yaml](../../tests/ignition/compose.yaml) pins
35. `inductiveautomation/ignition:8.3.8`, and bind-mounts two host directories:
36. 
37. | Host path | Container path | Purpose |
38. |---|---|---|
39. | `tests/ignition/seed/data` | `/usr/local/bin/ignition/data` | The Gateway's live data directory — raw files copied out of a configured container with `docker cp`. This is what makes the `Logix-Verification` project and its tag/device configuration persist and stay directly editable. |
40. | `tests/ignition/gwbk` | `/backups` (read-only) | Holds a checked-in `.gwbk` Gateway backup that can restore a fresh Gateway. Set `GATEWAY_RESTORE=/backups/<file>.gwbk` in `compose.yaml` to auto-restore on first boot of an empty `seed/data`. |
41. 
42. Neither directory is committed by default (raw Gateway data is a mutable local working copy, not
43. a source artifact) except the `.gwbk` backup, which is the durable, reviewable snapshot.
44. 
45. The API reference for the Gateway's config/scripting REST API is
46. [tests/ignition/ignition-openapi.json](../../tests/ignition/ignition-openapi.json) (large;
47. `grep` it rather than opening it whole). All API calls below need the header:
48. 
49. ```text
50. X-Ignition-API-Token: Logix-Verification:qvJOLBrJNAFWrDgpYhtTBpKeGyPB1l6HxAabyf8SUjA
51. ```
52. 
53. ## Start
54. 
55. Set the EULA flag only after review. Optionally supply `GATEWAY_ADMIN_PASSWORD` in the current
56. shell; if omitted, Compose uses the default (`password`).
57. 
58. ```powershell
59. $env:ACCEPT_IGNITION_EULA = "Y"
60. docker compose -f tests\ignition\compose.yaml up -d
61. ```
62. 
63. Wait for the Gateway to accept API calls (module loading takes roughly a minute on first boot):
64. 
65. ```powershell
66. do {
67.     Start-Sleep -Seconds 5
68.     $status = (curl.exe -s -o NUL -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:9088/StatusPing)
69. } while ($status -ne "200")
70. ```
71. 
72. Open the project in a browser at:
73. 
74. ```text
75. http://localhost:9088/data/perspective/client/Logix-Verification/logix-verification
76. ```
77. 
78. ## Verification procedure
79. 
80. Each PLC change under review follows this sequence. Steps 1–3 are one-time or per-change
81. Gateway configuration (done through the Gateway web UI at `http://localhost:9088`, or the config
82. REST API below); step 4 reloads the change; step 5 hands the session to the human reviewer.
83. 
84. ### 1. Set up the Logix device connection to talk to the Echo emulator
85. 
86. In the Gateway web UI: **Config \> OPC UA \> Devices \> Create new Device \> Allen-Bradley Logix
87. Driver**. Point the connection at the Echo chassis's `EmulateEthernet\<ip>` comm path (see
88. [windows-runner-setup.md](windows-runner-setup.md) for how the non-loopback adapter IP is
89. assigned). Confirm the device reaches **Connected** status before continuing.
90. 
91. Equivalently, via the config API (`PUT /data/api/v1/resources/com.inductiveautomation.opcua/device`)
92. using the `X-Ignition-API-Token` header above — see the `device` tag in
93. [ignition-openapi.json](../../tests/ignition/ignition-openapi.json) for the request schema.
94. 
95. ### 2. Add the tags needed to read for human verification
96. 
97. Add or update OPC tags in the `Logix-Verification` project's tag provider for every input and
98. output referenced by the change record, bound to the device from step 1. Do not invent tag paths —
99. read them from the exploded `src/` tree for the controller under review (per
100. [l5x-source.instructions.md](../../.github/instructions/l5x-source.instructions.md)). Use the
101. Gateway UI's Tag Browser, or `PUT /data/api/v1/resources/ignition/tag-provider` /
102. `POST /data/api/v1/tags/import` for scripted updates.
103. 
104. ### 3. Modify the `logix-verification` view to include all the variables used in the testing setup
105. 
106. Edit the Perspective view at
107. `tests/ignition/seed/data/projects/Logix-Verification/com.inductiveautomation.perspective/views/logix-verification/view.json`
108. (or the Designer) so every tag added in step 2 has a bound component — readouts for outputs,
109. input controls for anything the reviewer needs to change. Keep the view scoped to the current
110. change; remove bindings for tags that are no longer relevant so the reviewer isn't looking at
111. stale data.
112. 
113. ### 4. Initiate a project scan to load in the changed files
114. 
115. Because the view and tag files were edited directly on disk, tell the Gateway to pick them up:
116. 
117. ```powershell
118. curl.exe -X POST `
119.   -H "X-Ignition-API-Token: Logix-Verification:qvJOLBrJNAFWrDgpYhtTBpKeGyPB1l6HxAabyf8SUjA" `
120.   http://localhost:9088/data/api/v1/scan/projects
121. ```
122. 
123. Poll `GET /data/api/v1/scan/projects` (same header) until `scanActive` is `false`, then confirm
124. `lastScanTimestamp` advanced. If a resource lock is held, `POST` also releases it.
125. 
126. ### 5. Inform the user the verification view is ready for review
127. 
128. Once the scan completes, tell the reviewer the view is ready and share the URL:
129. 
130. ```text
131. http://localhost:9088/data/perspective/client/Logix-Verification/logix-verification
132. ```
133. 
134. ## Review procedure
135. 
136. The reviewer works directly in the `logix-verification` Perspective view: adjust any bound
137. input controls, observe the bound output readouts, and compare against the change record's
138. expected behavior. This is a human observation, not an automated pass/fail — the persisted HTML
139. report from the YAML/Echo run in [tests/cases/](../../tests/cases) remains the auditable
140. expected-versus-actual automated evidence.
141. 
142. ## Stop
143. 
144. ```powershell
145. docker compose -f tests\ignition\compose.yaml down
146. ```
147. 
148. `tests/ignition/seed/data` is retained on disk for faster later startup, so tags, the device
149. connection, and view edits persist across restarts. Remove it explicitly when a clean Gateway is
150. required (for example, to test restoring `tests/ignition/gwbk/*.gwbk` from scratch):
151. 
152. ```powershell
153. Remove-Item tests\ignition\seed\data -Recurse -Force
154. ```
155. 
156. ## Troubleshooting
157. 
158. | Symptom | Action |
159. |---|---|

 # Ignition Perspective Human Verification
 
 Use this optional test-only session when a reviewer wants to adjust approved PLC inputs and see
 the resulting Logix Echo readbacks in a browser. Automated YAML cases remain the release gate.
 This session is not a production HMI, commissioning substitute, or safety-validation tool.
 
 ## Architecture
 
 ```text
 Perspective browser
         |
 Ignition Gateway 8.3.8 in Docker (project "Logix-Verification")
         | OPC UA device connection
 FactoryTalk Logix Echo controller (ControlLogix 5580 emulation)
 ```
 
 The Gateway runs from a single, hand-configured project named **`Logix-Verification`** with a
 Perspective view named **`logix-verification`**. Unlike a generated one-off project, this Gateway
 keeps a real Logix device connection so a reviewer (or an agent, via the Gateway config API) can
 add tags and wire them into the view for whatever change is under review. There is no separate
 Windows bridge process for this flow — Ignition talks to Echo directly over OPC UA/EtherNet-IP,
 the same as it would talk to a physical controller.
 
 ## Prerequisites
 
 - Complete [windows-runner-setup.md](windows-runner-setup.md), including the non-loopback Echo
   adapter and Rockwell VCS tools.
 - Install Docker Desktop with Linux containers and either `docker compose` or `docker-compose`.
 - Keep host port `9088` (HTTP) and `8043` (HTTPS) available, or set `IGNITION_HTTP_PORT` /
   `IGNITION_HTTPS_PORT` before starting.
 - Review the [Ignition Docker image documentation](https://www.docs.inductiveautomation.com/docs/8.1/platform/docker-image)
   and the Inductive Automation EULA before accepting it.
 
 The Compose service in [compose.yaml](../../tests/ignition/compose.yaml) pins
 `inductiveautomation/ignition:8.3.8`, and bind-mounts two host directories:
 
 | Host path | Container path | Purpose |
 |---|---|---|
 | `tests/ignition/seed/data` | `/usr/local/bin/ignition/data` | The Gateway's live data directory — raw files copied out of a configured container with `docker cp`. This is what makes the `Logix-Verification` project and its tag/device configuration persist and stay directly editable. |
 | `tests/ignition/gwbk` | `/backups` (read-only) | Holds a checked-in `.gwbk` Gateway backup that can restore a fresh Gateway. Set `GATEWAY_RESTORE=/backups/<file>.gwbk` in `compose.yaml` to auto-restore on first boot of an empty `seed/data`. |
 
 Neither directory is committed by default (raw Gateway data is a mutable local working copy, not
 a source artifact) except the `.gwbk` backup, which is the durable, reviewable snapshot.
 
 The API reference for the Gateway's config/scripting REST API is
 [tests/ignition/ignition-openapi.json](../../tests/ignition/ignition-openapi.json) (large;
 `grep` it rather than opening it whole). All API calls below need the header:
 
 ```text
 X-Ignition-API-Token: Logix-Verification:qvJOLBrJNAFWrDgpYhtTBpKeGyPB1l6HxAabyf8SUjA
 ```
 
 ## Start
 
 Set the EULA flag only after review. Optionally supply `GATEWAY_ADMIN_PASSWORD` in the current
 shell; if omitted, Compose uses the default (`password`).
 
 ```powershell
 $env:ACCEPT_IGNITION_EULA = "Y"
 docker compose -f tests\ignition\compose.yaml up -d
 ```
 
 Wait for the Gateway to accept API calls (module loading takes roughly a minute on first boot):
 
 ```powershell
 do {
     Start-Sleep -Seconds 5
     $status = (curl.exe -s -o NUL -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:9088/StatusPing)
 } while ($status -ne "200")
 ```
 
 Open the project in a browser at:
 
 ```text
 http://localhost:9088/data/perspective/client/Logix-Verification/logix-verification
 ```
 
 ## Verification procedure
 
 Each PLC change under review follows this sequence. Steps 1–3 are one-time or per-change
 Gateway configuration (done through the Gateway web UI at `http://localhost:9088`, or the config
 REST API below); step 4 reloads the change; step 5 hands the session to the human reviewer.
 
 ### 1. Set up the Logix device connection to talk to the Echo emulator
 
 In the Gateway web UI: **Config \> OPC UA \> Devices \> Create new Device \> Allen-Bradley Logix
 Driver**. Point the connection at the Echo chassis's `EmulateEthernet\<ip>` comm path (see
 [windows-runner-setup.md](windows-runner-setup.md) for how the non-loopback adapter IP is
 assigned). Confirm the device reaches **Connected** status before continuing.
 
 Equivalently, via the config API (`PUT /data/api/v1/resources/com.inductiveautomation.opcua/device`)
 using the `X-Ignition-API-Token` header above — see the `device` tag in
 [ignition-openapi.json](../../tests/ignition/ignition-openapi.json) for the request schema.
 
 ### 2. Add the tags needed to read for human verification
 
 Add or update OPC tags in the `Logix-Verification` project's tag provider for every input and
 output referenced by the change record, bound to the device from step 1. Do not invent tag paths —
 read them from the exploded `src/` tree for the controller under review (per
 [l5x-source.instructions.md](../../.github/instructions/l5x-source.instructions.md)). Use the
 Gateway UI's Tag Browser, or `PUT /data/api/v1/resources/ignition/tag-provider` /
 `POST /data/api/v1/tags/import` for scripted updates.
 
 ### 3. Modify the `logix-verification` view to include all the variables used in the testing setup
 
 Edit the Perspective view at
 `tests/ignition/seed/data/projects/Logix-Verification/com.inductiveautomation.perspective/views/logix-verification/view.json`
 (or the Designer) so every tag added in step 2 has a bound component — readouts for outputs,
 input controls for anything the reviewer needs to change. Keep the view scoped to the current
 change; remove bindings for tags that are no longer relevant so the reviewer isn't looking at
 stale data.
 
 ### 4. Initiate a project scan to load in the changed files
 
 Because the view and tag files were edited directly on disk, tell the Gateway to pick them up:
 
 ```powershell
 curl.exe -X POST `
   -H "X-Ignition-API-Token: Logix-Verification:qvJOLBrJNAFWrDgpYhtTBpKeGyPB1l6HxAabyf8SUjA" `
   http://localhost:9088/data/api/v1/scan/projects
 ```
 
 Poll `GET /data/api/v1/scan/projects` (same header) until `scanActive` is `false`, then confirm
 `lastScanTimestamp` advanced. If a resource lock is held, `POST` also releases it.
 
 ### 5. Inform the user the verification view is ready for review
 
 Once the scan completes, tell the reviewer the view is ready and share the URL:
 
 ```text
 http://localhost:9088/data/perspective/client/Logix-Verification/logix-verification
 ```
 
 ## Review procedure
 
 The reviewer works directly in the `logix-verification` Perspective view: adjust any bound
 input controls, observe the bound output readouts, and compare against the change record's
 expected behavior. This is a human observation, not an automated pass/fail — the persisted HTML
 report from the YAML/Echo run in [tests/cases/](../../tests/cases) remains the auditable
 expected-versus-actual automated evidence.
 
 ## Stop
 
 ```powershell
 docker compose -f tests\ignition\compose.yaml down
 ```
 
 `tests/ignition/seed/data` is retained on disk for faster later startup, so tags, the device
 connection, and view edits persist across restarts. Remove it explicitly when a clean Gateway is
 required (for example, to test restoring `tests/ignition/gwbk/*.gwbk` from scratch):
 
 ```powershell
 Remove-Item tests\ignition\seed\data -Recurse -Force
 ```
 
 ## Troubleshooting
 
 | Symptom | Action |
 |---|---|
 | `docker` not found | Install or start Docker Desktop, then confirm `docker compose version` |
 | Gateway never reaches `StatusPing` | Run `docker compose -f tests/ignition/compose.yaml logs gateway` |
 | Config API returns 503 | The Gateway is still loading modules; wait and retry `StatusPing` before calling `/data/api/v1/*` |
 | Config API returns 401/403 | Confirm the `X-Ignition-API-Token` header exactly matches the token configured on the `Logix-Verification` project |
 | Device connection never reaches Connected | Confirm the Echo chassis's `EmulateEthernet\<ip>` comm path and that the non-loopback adapter from [windows-runner-setup.md](windows-runner-setup.md) is up |
 | Project scan does not pick up view/tag edits | Confirm files were saved under `tests/ignition/seed/data/projects/Logix-Verification/`, then re-run `POST /data/api/v1/scan/projects` |
 
 `tests/ignition/seed/data` is a mutable local working copy, not a source artifact, and must not be
 committed. Only `tests/ignition/gwbk/*.gwbk` backups are meant to be checked in as durable,
 reviewable snapshots.

<ask_user>
Use the ask_user tool to ask the user clarifying questions when needed.

**IMPORTANT: Never ask questions via plain text output.** When you need input from the user, use this tool instead of asking in your response text. The tool provides a better UX and ensures the user's answer is captured properly.

Guidelines:
- Prefer multiple choice (provide choices array) over freeform for faster UX
- Do NOT include "Other", "Something else", or similar catch-all choices - the UI automatically adds a freeform input option
- Only use pure freeform (no choices) when the answer truly cannot be predicted
- Ask one question at a time - do not batch multiple questions
- Don't ask the questions in bullet points or numbered lists. Ask each question in a clear sentence or paragraph form.
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first choice and add "(Recommended)" to the label
  Example: choices: ["PostgreSQL (Recommended)", "MySQL", "SQLite"]

Examples:
1. BAD - bundling multiple questions into one and asking the user to confirm or break them apart:
  { "question": "Here's what I'm thinking:\n1. Use PostgreSQL for the database\n2. Add Redis for caching\n3. Use JWT for auth\nDoes this sound good, or would you like to discuss each choice individually?", "choices": ["Sounds good", "Let's discuss individually"] }
  WORKAROUND - ask one focused question per tool call:
  First call:  { "question": "What database should I use?", "choices": ["PostgreSQL", "MySQL", "SQLite"] }
  Second call: { "question": "Should I add Redis for caching?", "choices": ["Yes", "No"] }
  Third call:  { "question": "What auth strategy should I use?", "choices": ["JWT", "Session-based", "OAuth"] }
2. BAD - embedding choices in the question text instead of using the choices field:
  { "question": "What database should I use? (PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQLite)" }
  WORKAROUND - put the options in the choices array:
  { "question": "What database should I use?", "choices": ["PostgreSQL", "MySQL", "SQLite"] }

When to STOP and ask (do not assume):
- Design decisions that significantly affect implementation approach
- Behavioral questions (e.g., "should this be unlimited or capped?")
- Scope ambiguity (e.g., which features to include/exclude)
- Edge cases where multiple reasonable approaches exist

<sql>
**Session database** (database: "session", the default):
The per-session database persists across the session but is isolated from other sessions.

**When to use SQL vs plan.md:**
- Use plan.md for prose: problem statements, approach notes, high-level planning
- Use SQL for operational data: todo lists, test cases, batch items, status tracking

**Pre-existing tables (ready to use):**
- `todos`: id, title, description, status (pending/in_progress/done/blocked), created_at, updated_at
- `todo_deps`: todo_id, depends_on (for dependency tracking)

**Todo tracking workflow:**
Use descriptive kebab-case IDs (not t1, t2). Write titles in gerund form (e.g. "Creating user auth module"). Include enough detail that the todo can be executed without referring back to the plan:
```sql
INSERT INTO todos (id, title, description) VALUES
  ('user-auth', 'Creating user auth module', 'Implement JWT auth in src/auth/ so login, logout, and token refresh don''t depend on server sessions. Use bcrypt for password hashing.');
```

**Todo status workflow:**
- `pending`: Todo is waiting to be started
- `in_progress`: You are actively working on this todo (set this before starting!)
- `done`: Todo is complete
- `blocked`: Todo cannot proceed (document why in description)

**IMPORTANT: Always update todo status as you work:**
1. Before starting a todo: `UPDATE todos SET status = 'in_progress' WHERE id = 'X'`
2. After completing a todo: `UPDATE todos SET status = 'done' WHERE id = 'X'`
3. Check todo_status in each user message to see what's ready

**Dependencies:** Insert into todo_deps when one todo must complete before another:
```sql
INSERT INTO todo_deps (todo_id, depends_on) VALUES ('api-routes', 'user-model');  -- routes wait for model
```

**Create any tables you need.** The database is yours to use for any purpose:
- Load and query data (CSVs, API responses, file listings)
- Track progress on batch operations
- Store intermediate results for multi-step analysis
- Any workflow where SQL queries would help

Common patterns:

1. **Todo tracking with dependencies:**
```sql
-- todos and todo_deps already exist — do NOT CREATE them, just INSERT:
INSERT INTO todos (id, title, description) VALUES ('user-model', 'Creating user model', 'Define the User schema and relations in src/models/user.ts');

-- Find todos with no pending dependencies ("ready" query):
SELECT t.* FROM todos t
WHERE t.status = 'pending'
AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM todo_deps td
    JOIN todos dep ON td.depends_on = dep.id
    WHERE td.todo_id = t.id AND dep.status != 'done'
);
```

2. **TDD test case tracking:**
```sql
CREATE TABLE test_cases (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    status TEXT DEFAULT 'not_written'
);
SELECT * FROM test_cases WHERE status = 'not_written' LIMIT 1;
UPDATE test_cases SET status = 'written' WHERE id = 'tc1';
```

3. **Batch item processing (e.g., PR comments):**
```sql
CREATE TABLE review_items (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    file_path TEXT,
    comment TEXT,
    status TEXT DEFAULT 'pending'
);
SELECT * FROM review_items WHERE status = 'pending' AND file_path = 'src/auth.ts';
UPDATE review_items SET status = 'addressed' WHERE id IN ('r1', 'r2');
```

4. **Session state (key-value):**
```sql
CREATE TABLE session_state (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT);
INSERT OR REPLACE INTO session_state (key, value) VALUES ('current_phase', 'testing');
SELECT value FROM session_state WHERE key = 'current_phase';
```
</sql>

**When to Use Sub-Agents**
* Use a matching specialist when the request specifically calls for that domain expertise.
* For other reviews, audits, and summaries, never delegate parts of a codebase that is small enough to read directly, regardless of how it divides into separate areas; do them yourself. Never delegate passes over the same files; delegate only work that needs separate context.

**When to use explore agent** (not grep/glob):
* Never use explore to split a review, audit, or summary by labeled area when its total scope is small; do it yourself. Reserve explore for independent threads that need substantial separate context.
* For simple lookups — understanding a specific component, finding a symbol, or reading a few known files — do it yourself using grep/glob/view. This is faster and keeps context in your conversation.
* Trace a single continuous chain yourself.
* Do not speculatively launch explore agents in the background "just in case" — they consume resources and rarely finish before you've already found the answer yourself.

**If you do use explore:**
* The explore agent is stateless — provide complete context in each call.
* Batch related questions into one call. Launch independent explorations in parallel.
* Do NOT duplicate its work by calling grep/view on files it already reported.
* Once you have enough information to address the user's request, stop investigating and deliver the result. Don't chase every lead or do redundant follow-up searches.

**When to use custom agents**:
* If both a built-in agent and a custom agent could handle a task, prefer the custom agent as it has specialized knowledge for this environment.

**How to Use Sub-Agents**
* Instruct the sub-agent to do the task itself, not just give advice.
* Once you delegate a scope to an agent, that agent owns it until it completes or fails; do not investigate the same scope yourself.
* If a sub-agent fails repeatedly, do the task yourself.
**Avoiding Unnecessary Sub-Agent Delegation**
* Before delegating, assess whether a direct approach (1-2 tool calls with grep/glob/view) would be faster. Only delegate tasks that genuinely benefit from multi-step autonomous work.
* If a sub-agent completes with 0 useful turns or produces no actionable output, do not re-launch it — fall back to doing the work yourself immediately.

**Background Agents**
* After launching a background agent for work you need before your next step, tell the user you're waiting, then end your response with no tool calls. A completion notification will arrive automatically.
* When that notification arrives, a good default is to call read_agent once with wait: true to retrieve the result. If it still shows running, stop there for this response. Leave same-scope work with the agent while it runs.
* Use read_agent for completed background agents, not to check whether they're done.

**Multi-Turn Conversations**
* Background agents stay alive after responding. Instead of launching a new agent, send follow-up messages with write_agent to refine, correct, or extend the agent's work.
* Prefer write_agent for iterative refinement over launching a new agent — the agent retains its full conversation context.
* Typical workflow: start agent (background) → wait for completion notification → read_agent (get result) → write_agent (send refinement) → wait for notification → read_agent (get updated result).
* Use read_agent with since_turn as an inclusive 0-based start turn.
* Idle agents (status: "idle") are waiting for messages — they're ready to receive write_agent immediately.
</task>

<custom_instruction>
# ACS-Logix-AI-Flow — Repository Instructions

This repository is a **Rockwell Automation PLC programming assistant workspace**. It holds
change records, testing assets, tooling, and documentation for Logix workflows; production
controller source is intentionally kept out of origin. The workspace can temporarily host local
controller trees for analysis or test preparation, but those trees are not committed. The repo
also includes a curated knowledge corpus, a RAG index over that corpus, automated tests that run
against FactoryTalk Logix Echo, and a CI/CD pipeline modelled
on Rockwell publication `LOGIX-AT002A-EN-P` and `github.com/RockwellAutomation/ra-logix-cicd`.

## Ground rules

1. **Controller code is safety-relevant.** Never speculate about logic behaviour. If the
   intent of a rung, routine, or interlock is not evident from the source, say so and ask.
2. **Search the knowledge base before answering.** Use the `logix-kb` MCP server
   (`search_knowledge`) or read under `docs/`. Cite the file you relied on.
3. **Never hand-edit assembled artifacts.** `build/` is generated. Edit the Rockwell VCS tree
   under `src/`, then run `l5xgit implode` through `tools/logix/acd.ps1`.
4. **Every functional change starts as a change request.** See
   [docs/workflow/change-lifecycle.md](../docs/workflow/change-lifecycle.md).
5. **Do not invent tag names, module catalog numbers, or AOI signatures.** Read them from
   `src/`. A wrong tag name is a machine fault, not a compile error.
6. **Do not commit real controller trees to origin.** `src/controllers/` is for local,
   temporary working copies only. Verified technicians apply version control on target systems
   with the separate implementation tooling.

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `src/controllers/<name>/` | Local-only Rockwell VCS exploded tree used temporarily for analysis/build steps; do not commit production controller content |
| `src/library/` | Shared AOI definitions and UDTs promoted for reuse across controllers |
| `build/` | Generated full-application `.L5X` / `.ACD` — git-ignored |
| `docs/` | Curated knowledge corpus (this is what the RAG index ingests) |
| `tools/logix/` | Rockwell VCS wrappers, ACD builds, deployment resolution, and plan validation |
| `tools/rag/` | Corpus ingest, vector index, query CLI, MCP server |
| `tests/cases/` | YAML test plans consumed by the harness |
| `tests/harness/` | .NET 10 console harness over EchoSDK + LDSDK |
| `changes/` | One markdown record per change request |

## Toolchain facts

- Studio 5000 Logix Designer **v38.00.00+**, FactoryTalk Logix Echo **4.00.00+**.
- Rockwell VCS tools revision `d10fae3d35b240ca6bf38fe83ec633b02ae5b9dc`; configure
   `ACS_L5XGIT_PATH` or put `l5xgit` on `PATH`.
- LDSDK package `RockwellAutomation.LogixDesigner.CSClient`, EchoSDK package
  `RockwellAutomation.FactoryTalkLogixEcho.Api.Client`. Both are **local `.nupkg` files**, not
  on nuget.org — see [docs/runbooks/windows-runner-setup.md](../docs/runbooks/windows-runner-setup.md).
- Logix Echo emulates **ControlLogix 5580** only.
- Echo comm path format is `EmulateEthernet\<ip>`.
- Studio 5000, Echo, and both SDKs are **Windows-only**. The Python tooling is cross-platform;
  everything else requires the self-hosted Windows runner.

## Language conventions

- **Structured Text** — see [docs/standards/structured-text-style.md](../docs/standards/structured-text-style.md).
- **Python** (`tools/`) — 3.11+, PEP 8, type hints, `pathlib`, `logging`. No bare `except`.
- **C#** (`tests/harness/`) — .NET 10, nullable enabled, `async`/`await` throughout, no `.Result`
  on SDK calls except where the Rockwell reference does so in synchronous helpers.
- **YAML test plans** — schema in [docs/testing/test-case-format.md](../docs/testing/test-case-format.md).

## When asked to make a change

Follow this order. Do not skip steps.

1. Restate the requested behaviour change in control terms (what tags, what conditions, what
   equipment states).
2. Locate the affected components in `src/` and read them.
3. Write or update the change record in `changes/`.
4. Edit the Rockwell VCS source under `RSLogix5000Content/`.
5. Add or update a YAML test case in `tests/cases/` that would fail before the change and pass
   after it.
6. Run `pwsh tools/logix/acd.ps1 -FromDir src/controllers/<Name> -ToL5X build/<Name>.L5X
   -Force` to prove Rockwell's tooling can implode the tree.
7. Summarise: files touched, tags added/removed, test coverage, residual risk.

## Never

- Never commit `.ACD` files (binary, unmergeable) — they are build outputs.
- Never commit production controller source under `src/controllers/`; keep those trees local and ephemeral.
- Never change `ExternalAccess`, `Constant`, or safety task assignment without calling it out
  explicitly in the change record.
- Never delete a tag that is referenced anywhere in `src/` without listing every reference first.
- Never disable a test to make the pipeline pass.

**Organization & Style**

* Prefer clarity over cleverness. Write small, single-purpose functions with descriptive names. Use guard clauses and early returns.
* Keep dependencies minimal and portable. Default to standard libraries when practical.
* Favor immutability and pure functions when reasonable; isolate side effects at boundaries.
* Comments explain **why**, not **what**. Keep them concise. Public functions include brief docstrings with inputs/outputs and edge cases.

**Languages**

* **Python 3.x**: Follow PEP 8. Use type hints. Prefer `pathlib`, f-strings, and `logging`. Provide docstring examples where helpful.
* **Jython 2.7 (Ignition scripting)**: Remain Python-2.7 compatible (no f-strings/`pathlib`/type hints). Use `system.*` APIs, avoid blocking the UI thread, and write thread-safe gateway/event scripts.
* **Java** (Ignition modules/SDK): Prefer clear composition over inheritance. Use standard logging. Avoid heavy frameworks.
* **TypeScript/JavaScript**: Default to TypeScript with strict typing. Use modern ES modules, async/await, and functional React components with hooks.
* **SQL**: Be explicit and readable. Use parameterized queries always. Name columns clearly; prefer UTC timestamps.
* **PowerShell/YAML/JSON/HTML/CSS**: Emphasize portability and readability. Validate inputs; keep configs declarative.

**Frameworks & Ecosystem**

* **Ignition 8.1 (Vision/Perspective, Gateway scripts, Tag Change, Alarm Pipelines)**:

  * Use system functions (`system.tag`, `system.db`, `system.alarm`, etc.).
  * Make long-running work asynchronous or gateway-scoped; handle retries with exponential backoff.
  * Never hard-code credentials or gateway paths; centralize configuration.
* **React + TypeScript** (for web tools/dashboards):

  * Functional components, hooks, and composition. Keep components small and testable.
  * State co-located or lifted thoughtfully; avoid unnecessary global state.
* **M365/SharePoint/Power Automate** (scripts/tools):

  * Prefer API-first, least-privilege access; handle token refresh and throttling.
  * Keep tenant/site IDs, list names, and secrets out of code; use env/config.

**Error Handling & Logging**

* Fail fast on invalid inputs. Validate early.
* Log actionable messages (who/what/where) with levels (INFO/WARN/ERROR).
* Surface human-readable errors; include remediation hints.

**Security & Data**

* No plaintext secrets, tokens, or connection strings in code or logs.
* Parameterize SQL; never string-concatenate queries.
* Sanitize/validate all external inputs (forms, params, files, tags).

**Testing & Maintainability**

* Write code that’s unit-test friendly: dependency injection, pure functions, stable interfaces.
* Provide small usage examples in docstrings where helpful.
* Prefer deterministic behavior; avoid hidden globals and time-dependent logic.

**Performance & Reliability**

* Readability first; optimize hotspots only with evidence.
* Use timeouts and bounded retries with jitter for I/O.
* Aim for idempotent operations, especially in automation and SCADA contexts.

**Conventions**

* Python: `snake_case` for functions/variables, `PascalCase` for classes.
* TypeScript/JS: `camelCase` for variables/functions, `PascalCase` for components.
* Timestamps stored/handled in **UTC**; when interacting with existing tables, prefer the canonical timestamp column name `Time_Stamp` when applicable.

**Behavior**

* When requirements are ambiguous, propose a clear, minimal default and annotate assumptions.
* Prefer explicit configuration and clear interfaces over “magic.”
* Generate code that’s consistent, documented, and easy to extend.

data.summaryContent:
<overview>
The user is setting up a Docker-based Ignition Gateway 8.3.8 test environment for human verification of Logix PLC changes against a FactoryTalk Logix Echo emulator, replacing an earlier bridge-based architecture. My role has evolved from fixing Docker Compose syntax bugs, to redesigning the data-persistence strategy (from a seed-init container to a directly-editable bind-mounted data directory copied from a hand-configured Gateway), to writing a runbook documenting the 5-step verification workflow, and now to proving out the actual REST API calls against the live Gateway to add an Echo Logix device connection.
</history>
1. User reported `docker compose up` failing with `[: -c: line 2: syntax error: unexpected end of file]` in the `ignition-init` service.
   - Diagnosed: Compose's shorthand `command: >-` (a plain multi-line string) gets word-split into a list of args before being passed to `bash -c`, breaking the `if/then/fi` script.
   - Fixed by changing `command` to a YAML list with one string element in [compose.yaml](c:\Users\MitchellLandreth\Git-Local\AB-Logix-CI-CD\tests\ignition\compose.yaml).
   - Verified with `docker compose config` and `docker compose up ignition-init` — succeeded.

2. User ran full `docker compose up` and got a new error: `cp: cannot stat '/usr/local/bin/ignition/data/gateway.xml_clean': No such file or directory`.
   - Root cause: a stale `.gitkeep` file in the seed target made `ls -A` non-empty, so the init container's "already populated" check skipped seeding entirely on a fresh checkout.
   - Fixed the seed check to exclude `.gitkeep` via `grep -v '^\.gitkeep$'`.
   - Next error: `cp: preserving times for '/seed-target/.': Operation not permitted` — Windows bind mounts don't support `cp -a`'s timestamp preservation. Switched to `cp -r`.
   - Next error: `chmod: changing permissions of '/seed-target': Operation not permitted` — the bind-mount root itself can't be chmod'd on Windows. Attempted `find /seed-target -mindepth 1 -exec chmod a+rwX {} +` to skip the root, but this line of work was abandoned before final verification when the user requested a different approach entirely (see request 3).

3. User explicitly requested to abandon the init-container/seeding approach and instead: "start a blank single gateway, and I will do the configuration we need and put a gateway backup file we can restore from in the future in `tests\ignition\gwbk`."
   - Rewrote [compose.yaml](c:\Users\MitchellLandreth\Git-Local\AB-Logix-CI-CD\tests\ignition\compose.yaml) to remove `ignition-init` entirely; `gateway` service now uses a named Docker volume (`ignition-data`) for `/usr/local/bin/ignition/data`, plus a read-only bind mount `./gwbk:/backups` with a commented-out `GATEWAY_RESTORE` env var for future restore.
   - Verified gateway boots healthy and responds 200 on `/StatusPing`.
   - Confirmed `tests/ignition/gwbk` already existed as an empty folder; no `.gitignore` changes needed since `tests/ignition/` is entirely untracked.

4. User did manual configuration in the Gateway UI (created project "Logix-Verification"), then said: "Since we will need access to the raw files to manipulate, copy the seed files from my ignition container in docker and use those. This is essentially what the gateway backup would contain." Also provided an `ignition-openapi.json` file, an API token (`X-Ignition-API-Token: Logix-Verification:qvJOLBrJNAFWrDgpYhtTBpKeGyPB1l6HxAabyf8SUjA`), project name (`Logix-Verification`), and view name (`logix-verification`). Requested instructions be added for a 5-step human-verification process: (1) set up Logix device connection to Echo, (2) add tags, (3) modify the `logix-verification` view, (4) initiate project scan, (5) inform user the view is ready.
   - Used `docker cp ignition-gateway-1:/usr/local/bin/ignition/data ./seed_tmp` to extract raw Gateway files, moved to `tests/ignition/seed/data`.
   - Confirmed the `Logix-Verification` project and its `.resources` dir existed in the copied seed, including a `view.json` at `tests/ignition/seed/data/projects/Logix-Verification/com.inductiveautomation.perspective/views/logix-verification/view.json`.
   - Updated [compose.yaml](c:\Users\MitchellLandreth\Git-Local\AB-Logix-CI-CD\tests\ignition\compose.yaml) to bind-mount `./seed/data:/usr/local/bin/ignition/data` (replacing the named volume) and kept `./gwbk:/backups:ro`.
   - Verified: brought stack down/up, confirmed gateway becomes healthy (~90 seconds to fully load modules) and the API token authenticates successfully against `GET /data/api/v1/projects/list` (returns the `Logix-Verification` project).
   - Explored `ignition-openapi.json` (12.7MB, must be grepped not fully read) to find relevant endpoints: `POST /data/api/v1/scan/projects` (scan trigger), `GET /data/api/v1/scan/projects` (scan status), `PUT /data/api/v1/resources/ignition/tag-provider` (tags), `PUT /data/api/v1/resources/com.inductiveautomation.opcua/device` (devices), `POST /data/api/v1/tags/import`.
   - Rewrote [docs/runbooks/ignition-human-verification.md](c:\Users\MitchellLandreth\Git-Local\AB-Logix-CI-CD\docs\runbooks\ignition-human-verification.md) completely: new Architecture section (Perspective → Ignition Gateway → OPC UA → Echo, no Windows bridge), new Prerequisites/table describing the two bind mounts, a `## Start` section using plain `docker compose up -d`, a `## Verification procedure` section with the 5 requested numbered steps (each grounded in real API endpoints/UI paths), updated `## Review procedure`, `## Stop`, and `## Troubleshooting` sections reflecting the new architecture (removed all references to the old bridge/token/ACD generation flow).
   - Noted to the user that [start-verification.ps1](c:\Users\MitchellLandreth\Git-Local\AB-Logix-CI-CD\tests\ignition\start-verification.ps1) and `stop-verification.ps1` still reference the old flow and are now stale, but left them untouched pending explicit instruction.

5. User's latest request: "The gateway has started, run the commands against the gateway for adding the echo logix device so we know that's working with the provided information."
   - Checked for `ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP` env var — not set locally.
   - Confirmed FactoryTalk Logix Echo Windows services ARE running (`FactoryTalk Logix Echo Message Broker`, `FactoryTalk Logix Echo Service`), but no chassis/IP was known.

<technical_details>
- **Docker Compose command word-splitting bug**: A YAML folded scalar (`command: >-`) is word-split by Compose before being passed to `entrypoint: ["/bin/bash", "-c"]`, breaking multi-line shell scripts with `if/fi`. Fix: wrap the script as a single-element YAML list: `command: ["- >-\n  <script>"]` style (i.e., `command:\n  - >-\n    <script>`).
- **`.gitkeep` breaks "is directory empty" checks**: `ls -A` includes dotfiles, so a placeholder `.gitkeep` (needed to keep an empty dir in git) will make an otherwise-empty seed target look "already populated." Must explicitly filter it out when checking, e.g. `ls -A dir | grep -v '^\.gitkeep$'`.
- **Windows bind-mount limitations**: `cp -a` (preserve mode/timestamps) fails with "Operation not permitted" against Windows-backed bind mounts inside Linux containers — use `cp -r` instead. Similarly, `chmod` on the bind-mount root directory itself fails ("Operation not permitted"), though `chmod` on files *inside* it can still work in some cases; this whole permission-wrangling approach was ultimately abandoned in favor of Docker-managed volumes / raw `docker cp` extraction (which sidesteps the Windows filesystem entirely since the container manages its own files, then `docker cp` snapshots them for reuse as a new bind mount).
- **Gateway boot timing**: After `docker compose up -d`, `/StatusPing` returns 200 well before the Config REST API (`/data/api/v1/*`) is ready — the API can return 503 for roughly 60-90 seconds after StatusPing succeeds while modules finish loading. Must poll and retry.
- **Ignition Config REST API structure** (from `ignition-openapi.json`, 12.7MB — always `grep`, never fully `view`):
  - `PUT /data/api/v1/resources/<module>/<resource-type>` — bulk modify/create resources (array body).
  - `GET /data/api/v1/resources/list/<module>/<resource-type>` — list existing resources (shows `signature` field on each item, e.g. `"683711fd9f5a02580b2455d8efdaba28fbbd32cc68ec07137338498403bf0e20"` — a long hex string, NOT simply zeros or empty).
  - `GET /data/api/v1/resources/find/<module>/<resource-type>/{name}` — 404s if resource doesn't exist yet.
  - `DELETE /data/api/v1/resources/<module>/<resource-type>/{name}/{signature}` — requires exact current signature.
  - `POST /data/api/v1/scan/projects` — triggers project filesystem scan; `GET` same path returns `{scanActive, lastScanTimestamp, lastScanDuration}`.
  - Device profile types include `LogixDriver`, `CompactLogix`, `ControlLogix`, `MicroLogix`, etc. `LogixDriver` schema: `config.settings.connectivity: {hostname (required), port (default 44818), localAddress, timeout (default 2000), connectionPath}`, `config.settings.advanced: {automaticRebrowseEnabled, identityRequestFrequency, cipConnectionSize, cipConnectionTimeout, slotNumber (default 0), concurrentRequests}`.
  - **UNRESOLVED**: The exact `signature` value required for a brand-new resource on `PUT` is still unknown. The field is `required` per error messages but existing resources show long hex signatures (~65 chars observed: `683711fd9f5a02580b2455d8efdaba28fbbd32cc68ec07137338498403bf0e20` — actually that's 65 hex chars, odd length, which contradicts the "string length not even" error seen for other attempts — this inconsistency itself is worth re-examining; possibly the "must be even" validation only applies to certain encodings or there's a leading/sentinel character). Need to check Inductive Automation's official Config API docs (web fetches to docs.inductiveautomation.com failed with 404s and search engines were blocked/unhelpful) or empirically test by first creating ANY resource successfully (e.g. via UI) then reading back its signature format, or check if there's a "create" convenience omitting signature validation via a different query param like `allowInvalidReferences` combined with something else, or check community/GitHub examples of the Ignition 8.3 config-management REST API for the exact create semantics.
  - No local Echo chassis/IP was previously configured; user manually supplied `192.168.127.5` as the IP to use for this test (per `ACS_LOGIX_ECHO_IP` convention documented in `windows-runner-setup.md`, though that env var itself was not set in this shell).
- Windows FactoryTalk Logix Echo services confirmed running via `Get-Service`: "FactoryTalk Logix Echo Message Broker" and "FactoryTalk Logix Echo Service".
</technical_details>

1. # Ignition Perspective Human Verification
2. 
3. Use this optional test-only session when a reviewer wants to adjust approved PLC inputs and see
4. the resulting Logix Echo readbacks in a browser. Automated YAML cases remain the release gate.
5. This session is not a production HMI, commissioning substitute, or safety-validation tool.
6. 
7. ## Architecture
8. 
9. ```text
10. Perspective browser
11.         |
12. Ignition Gateway 8.3.8 in Docker (project "Logix-Verification")
13.         | OPC UA device connection
14. FactoryTalk Logix Echo controller (ControlLogix 5580 emulation)
15. ```
16. 
17. The Gateway runs from a single, hand-configured project named **`Logix-Verification`** with a
18. Perspective view named **`logix-verification`**. Unlike a generated one-off project, this Gateway
19. keeps a real Logix device connection so a reviewer (or an agent, via the Gateway config API) can
20. add tags and wire them into the view for whatever change is under review. There is no separate
21. Windows bridge process for this flow — Ignition talks to Echo directly over OPC UA/EtherNet-IP,
22. the same as it would talk to a physical controller.
23. 
24. ## Prerequisites
25. 
26. - Complete [windows-runner-setup.md](windows-runner-setup.md), including the non-loopback Echo
27.   adapter and Rockwell VCS tools.
28. - Install Docker Desktop with Linux containers and either `docker compose` or `docker-compose`.
29. - Keep host port `9088` (HTTP) and `8043` (HTTPS) available, or set `IGNITION_HTTP_PORT` /
30.   `IGNITION_HTTPS_PORT` before starting.
31. - Review the [Ignition Docker image documentation](https://www.docs.inductiveautomation.com/docs/8.1/platform/docker-image)
32.   and the Inductive Automation EULA before accepting it.
33. 
34. The Compose service in [compose.yaml](../../tests/ignition/compose.yaml) pins
35. `inductiveautomation/ignition:8.3.8`, and bind-mounts two host directories:
36. 
37. | Host path | Container path | Purpose |
38. |---|---|---|
39. | `tests/ignition/seed/data` | `/usr/local/bin/ignition/data` | The Gateway's live data directory — raw files copied out of a configured container with `docker cp`. This is what makes the `Logix-Verification` project and its tag/device configuration persist and stay directly editable. |
40. | `tests/ignition/gwbk` | `/backups` (read-only) | Holds a checked-in `.gwbk` Gateway backup that can restore a fresh Gateway. Set `GATEWAY_RESTORE=/backups/<file>.gwbk` in `compose.yaml` to auto-restore on first boot of an empty `seed/data`. |
41. 
42. Neither directory is committed by default (raw Gateway data is a mutable local working copy, not
43. a source artifact) except the `.gwbk` backup, which is the durable, reviewable snapshot.
44. 
45. The API reference for the Gateway's config/scripting REST API is
46. [tests/ignition/ignition-openapi.json](../../tests/ignition/ignition-openapi.json) (large;
47. `grep` it rather than opening it whole). All API calls below need the header:
48. 
49. ```text
50. X-Ignition-API-Token: Logix-Verification:qvJOLBrJNAFWrDgpYhtTBpKeGyPB1l6HxAabyf8SUjA
51. ```
52. 
53. ## Start
54. 
55. Set the EULA flag only after review. Optionally supply `GATEWAY_ADMIN_PASSWORD` in the current
56. shell; if omitted, Compose uses the default (`password`).
57. 
58. ```powershell
59. $env:ACCEPT_IGNITION_EULA = "Y"
60. docker compose -f tests\ignition\compose.yaml up -d
61. ```
62. 
63. Wait for the Gateway to accept API calls (module loading takes roughly a minute on first boot):
64. 
65. ```powershell
66. do {
67.     Start-Sleep -Seconds 5
68.     $status = (curl.exe -s -o NUL -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:9088/StatusPing)
69. } while ($status -ne "200")
70. ```
71. 
72. Open the project in a browser at:
73. 
74. ```text
75. http://localhost:9088/data/perspective/client/Logix-Verification/logix-verification
76. ```
77. 
78. ## Verification procedure
79. 
80. Each PLC change under review follows this sequence. Steps 1–3 are one-time or per-change
81. Gateway configuration (done through the Gateway web UI at `http://localhost:9088`, or the config
82. REST API below); step 4 reloads the change; step 5 hands the session to the human reviewer.
83. 
84. ### 1. Set up the Logix device connection to talk to the Echo emulator
85. 
86. In the Gateway web UI: **Config \> OPC UA \> Devices \> Create new Device \> Allen-Bradley Logix
87. Driver**. Point the connection at the Echo chassis's `EmulateEthernet\<ip>` comm path (see
88. [windows-runner-setup.md](windows-runner-setup.md) for how the non-loopback adapter IP is
89. assigned). Confirm the device reaches **Connected** status before continuing.
90. 
91. Equivalently, via the config API (`PUT /data/api/v1/resources/com.inductiveautomation.opcua/device`)
92. using the `X-Ignition-API-Token` header above — see the `device` tag in
93. [ignition-openapi.json](../../tests/ignition/ignition-openapi.json) for the request schema.
94. 
95. ### 2. Add the tags needed to read for human verification
96. 
97. Add or update OPC tags in the `Logix-Verification` project's tag provider for every input and
98. output referenced by the change record, bound to the device from step 1. Do not invent tag paths —
99. read them from the exploded `src/` tree for the controller under review (per
100. [l5x-source.instructions.md](../../.github/instructions/l5x-source.instructions.md)). Use the
101. Gateway UI's Tag Browser, or `PUT /data/api/v1/resources/ignition/tag-provider` /
102. `POST /data/api/v1/tags/import` for scripted updates.
103. 
104. ### 3. Modify the `logix-verification` view to include all the variables used in the testing setup
105. 
106. Edit the Perspective view at
107. `tests/ignition/seed/data/projects/Logix-Verification/com.inductiveautomation.perspective/views/logix-verification/view.json`
108. (or the Designer) so every tag added in step 2 has a bound component — readouts for outputs,
109. input controls for anything the reviewer needs to change. Keep the view scoped to the current
110. change; remove bindings for tags that are no longer relevant so the reviewer isn't looking at
111. stale data.
112. 
113. ### 4. Initiate a project scan to load in the changed files
114. 
115. Because the view and tag files were edited directly on disk, tell the Gateway to pick them up:
116. 
117. ```powershell
118. curl.exe -X POST `
119.   -H "X-Ignition-API-Token: Logix-Verification:qvJOLBrJNAFWrDgpYhtTBpKeGyPB1l6HxAabyf8SUjA" `
120.   http://localhost:9088/data/api/v1/scan/projects
121. ```
122. 
123. Poll `GET /data/api/v1/scan/projects` (same header) until `scanActive` is `false`, then confirm
124. `lastScanTimestamp` advanced. If a resource lock is held, `POST` also releases it.
125. 
126. ### 5. Inform the user the verification view is ready for review
127. 
128. Once the scan completes, tell the reviewer the view is ready and share the URL:
129. 
130. ```text
131. http://localhost:9088/data/perspective/client/Logix-Verification/logix-verification
132. ```
133. 
134. ## Review procedure
135. 
136. The reviewer works directly in the `logix-verification` Perspective view: adjust any bound
137. input controls, observe the bound output readouts, and compare against the change record's
138. expected behavior. This is a human observation, not an automated pass/fail — the persisted HTML
139. report from the YAML/Echo run in [tests/cases/](../../tests/cases) remains the auditable
140. expected-versus-actual automated evidence.
141. 
142. ## Stop
143. 
144. ```powershell
145. docker compose -f tests\ignition\compose.yaml down
146. ```
147. 
148. `tests/ignition/seed/data` is retained on disk for faster later startup, so tags, the device
149. connection, and view edits persist across restarts. Remove it explicitly when a clean Gateway is
150. required (for example, to test restoring `tests/ignition/gwbk/*.gwbk` from scratch):
151. 
152. ```powershell
153. Remove-Item tests\ignition\seed\data -Recurse -Force
154. ```
155. 
156. ## Troubleshooting
157. 
158. | Symptom | Action |
159. |---|---|
160. | `docker` not found | Install or start Docker Desktop, then confirm `docker compose version` |
161. | Gateway never reaches `StatusPing` | Run `docker compose -f tests/ignition/compose.yaml logs gateway` |
162. | Config API returns 503 | The Gateway is still loading modules; wait and retry `StatusPing` before calling `/data/api/v1/*` |
163. | Config API returns 401/403 | Confirm the `X-Ignition-API-Token` header exactly matches the token configured on the `Logix-Verification` project |
164. | Device connection never reaches Connected | Confirm the Echo chassis's `EmulateEthernet\<ip>` comm path and that the non-loopback adapter from [windows-runner-setup.md](windows-runner-setup.md) is up |
165. | Project scan does not pick up view/tag edits | Confirm files were saved under `tests/ignition/seed/data/projects/Logix-Verification/`, then re-run `POST /data/api/v1/scan/projects` |
166. 
167. `tests/ignition/seed/data` is a mutable local working copy, not a source artifact, and must not be
168. committed. Only `tests/ignition/gwbk/*.gwbk` backups are meant to be checked in as durable,
169. reviewable snapshots.
170.

 Equivalently, via the config API (`PUT /data/api/v1/resources/com.inductiveautomation.opcua/device`)
 using the `X-Ignition-API-Token` header above — see the `device` tag in
 [ignition-openapi.json](../../tests/ignition/ignition-openapi.json) for the request schema.
 
 ### 2. Add the tags needed to read for human verification
 
 Add or update OPC tags in the `Logix-Verification` project's tag provider for every input and
 output referenced by the change record, bound to the device from step 1. Do not invent tag paths —
 read them from the exploded `src/` tree for the controller under review (per
 [l5x-source.instructions.md](../../.github/instructions/l5x-source.instructions.md)). Use the
 Gateway UI's Tag Browser, or `PUT /data/api/v1/resources/ignition/tag-provider` /
 `POST /data/api/v1/tags/import` for scripted updates.
 
 ### 3. Modify the `logix-verification` view to include all the variables used in the testing setup
 
 Edit the Perspective view at
 `tests/ignition/seed/data/projects/Logix-Verification/com.inductiveautomation.perspective/views/logix-verification/view.json`
 (or the Designer) so every tag added in step 2 has a bound component — readouts for outputs,
 input controls for anything the reviewer needs to change. Keep the view scoped to the current
 change; remove bindings for tags that are no longer relevant so the reviewer isn't looking at
 stale data.
 
 ### 4. Initiate a project scan to load in the changed files
 
 Because the view and tag files were edited directly on disk, tell the Gateway to pick them up:
 
 ```powershell
 curl.exe -X POST `
   -H "X-Ignition-API-Token: Logix-Verification:qvJOLBrJNAFWrDgpYhtTBpKeGyPB1l6HxAabyf8SUjA" `
   http://localhost:9088/data/api/v1/scan/projects
 ```
 
 Poll `GET /data/api/v1/scan/projects` (same header) until `scanActive` is `false`, then confirm
 `lastScanTimestamp` advanced. If a resource lock is held, `POST` also releases it.
 
 ### 5. Inform the user the verification view is ready for review
 
 Once the scan completes, tell the reviewer the view is ready and share the URL:
 
 ```text
 http://localhost:9088/data/perspective/client/Logix-Verification/logix-verification
 ```
 
 ## Review procedure
 
 The reviewer works directly in the `logix-verification` Perspective view: adjust any bound
 input controls, observe the bound output readouts, and compare against the change record's
 expected behavior. This is a human observation, not an automated pass/fail — the persisted HTML
 report from the YAML/Echo run in [tests/cases/](../../tests/cases) remains the auditable
 expected-versus-actual automated evidence.
 
 ## Stop
 
 ```powershell
 docker compose -f tests\ignition\compose.yaml down
 ```
 
 `tests/ignition/seed/data` is retained on disk for faster later startup, so tags, the device
 connection, and view edits persist across restarts. Remove it explicitly when a clean Gateway is
 required (for example, to test restoring `tests/ignition/gwbk/*.gwbk` from scratch):
 
 ```powershell
 Remove-Item tests\ignition\seed\data -Recurse -Force
 ```
 
 ## Troubleshooting
 
 | Symptom | Action |
 |---|---|
 | `docker` not found | Install or start Docker Desktop, then confirm `docker compose version` |
 | Gateway never reaches `StatusPing` | Run `docker compose -f tests/ignition/compose.yaml logs gateway` |
 | Config API returns 503 | The Gateway is still loading modules; wait and retry `StatusPing` before calling `/data/api/v1/*` |
 | Config API returns 401/403 | Confirm the `X-Ignition-API-Token` header exactly matches the token configured on the `Logix-Verification` project |
 | Device connection never reaches Connected | Confirm the Echo chassis's `EmulateEthernet\<ip>` comm path and that the non-loopback adapter from [windows-runner-setup.md](windows-runner-setup.md) is up |
 | Project scan does not pick up view/tag edits | Confirm files were saved under `tests/ignition/seed/data/projects/Logix-Verification/`, then re-run `POST /data/api/v1/scan/projects` |
 
 `tests/ignition/seed/data` is a mutable local working copy, not a source artifact, and must not be
 committed. Only `tests/ignition/gwbk/*.gwbk` backups are meant to be checked in as durable,
 reviewable snapshots.

arguments.old_str:
### 1. Set up the Logix device connection to talk to the Echo emulator

In the Gateway web UI: **Config \> OPC UA \> Devices \> Create new Device \> Allen-Bradley Logix
Driver**. Point the connection at the Echo chassis's `EmulateEthernet\<ip>` comm path (see
[windows-runner-setup.md](windows-runner-setup.md) for how the non-loopback adapter IP is
assigned). Confirm the device reaches **Connected** status before continuing.

Equivalently, via the config API (`PUT /data/api/v1/resources/com.inductiveautomation.opcua/device`)
using the `X-Ignition-API-Token` header above — see the `device` tag in
[ignition-openapi.json](../../tests/ignition/ignition-openapi.json) for the request schema.
arguments.new_str:
### 1. Set up the Logix device connection to talk to the Echo emulator

Use the Gateway web UI — it is more forgiving than the config API for first-time resource
creation (see the API note below):

1. Log in at `http://localhost:9088/data/app/login` (default `admin` / the `GATEWAY_ADMIN_PASSWORD`
   set at startup, `password` if unset).
2. Go to **Connections \> Devices \> Create Device Connection**.
3. Select **Allen-Bradley Logix Driver**, click **Next**.
4. Set **Name** (e.g. `EchoLogixVerification`) and **Hostname** to the Echo chassis's IP (see
   [windows-runner-setup.md](windows-runner-setup.md) for how the non-loopback adapter IP is
   assigned — the Windows host's own IP bound to Echo's `EmulateEthernet\<ip>` comm path, not a
   Docker-internal address). Leave Port `44818`, Timeout `2000`, Slot `0` unless the chassis says
   otherwise, then click **Create Device Connection**.
5. Confirm the device reaches **Connected** (not `ReconnectWait`) in the Devices list before
   continuing to step 2. If it doesn't, see Troubleshooting below — this almost always means the
   Echo chassis itself isn't started, not a Gateway config problem.

**API note — creating a *new* device via `PUT /data/api/v1/resources/com.inductiveautomation.opcua/device`
is not straightforward and the UI path above should be preferred for first-time creation:**

- The `signature` field is `required` in the request body even for brand-new resources, but the
  only value the Gateway accepts is a full 64-character lowercase hex string (any other length,
  including empty string, `null`, or omitting the field, returns `422`; even-length values that
  aren't a real signature return a bare `404` with no body — that 404 does **not** mean "invalid
  signature format accepted, resource not found", it means "route didn't match").
- `collection` must be `"core"`, not `"devices"` — confirmed by reading back a UI-created
  resource's `collection` field.
- Once a device exists, `GET /data/api/v1/resources/list/com.inductiveautomation.opcua/device`
  returns its real `signature` (e.g. `35721de688a9627d75276fd0f9d6045fe6138c9c466b9a355b879ae887bfd26f`,
  64 hex chars), which can then be reused for scripted `PUT` updates to that *same* resource
  (rename/reconfigure) or `DELETE .../device/{name}/{signature}` to remove it. There is no
  documented scripted "create" shortcut that avoids first creating the resource once through the
  UI (or Designer) to obtain its signature.
